text:
sasha: quick q — we pulled Boreal-13B and ran an int4 quantization / eval pass. the model card includes a "research-only, no commercial redistribution of weights" clause plus required attribution. can we (a) serve the quantized derivative from hosted API commercially, (b) hand over quantized weights to Dedicated customers, and (c) serve embeddings derived from the model to paying customers? :thinking:

sasha: license excerpt:
```
Model weights: RESEARCH USE ONLY. No commercial use. Redistribution of weights or derivatives prohibited. Attribution to BorealAI required for any public use.
```

kevin: context — we used the usual quant pipeline and produced artifacts:
```
python infra/tools/quantize.py --input ./models/boreal-13b --bits 4 --out ./artifacts/boreal-13b-int4.pt --preserve-ckpt-md5
# output: boreal-13b-int4.pt (4.2GB), eval logs in /runs/2026-03-18/quant-eval.log
```
kevin: perf: ~1.8x token/sec improvement, eval ppl +0.9, SFT head tests show ~2% drop on our safety prompts.

mike: we also ran embedding similarity tests — embeddings look near-identical for most queries, maybe small drift on niche legal queries. overall embeddings quality acceptable for prod.

jordan_legal: initial read — the clause you pasted is pretty explicit. high-level take: hosted commercial use would violate a "research-only / no commercial" restriction. handing out quantized weights to customers is redistribution of derivative weights -> also disallowed. embeddings are trickier: outputs (embeddings) are typically considered model outputs, not reproductions of weights, but the license language matters — if the license forbids "use" for commercial purposes, then serving embeddings commercially could still be considered a commercial use and thus prohibited.

jordan_legal: practical guidance:
- internal R&D and evals are fine under research-only.
- commercial hosting (hosted API paid access) -> NOT allowed without explicit upstream permission.
- Dedicated customers: giving them the quantized file is redistribution -> NOT allowed.
- embeddings: may be allowed in some cases if license only restricts redistribution of weights and not outputs, but in your quoted text it says "No commercial use" generally — that blocks it for commercial customers.

compliance-bot: posting internal template + link to policy: https://redwood.internal/legal/model-licenses — use the "Upstream Permission Request" template. fill in model tarball S3 link, quantization script, proposed use (hosted/dedicated/embeddings), and customer list.

amy: product question — is there a narrow permitted path: e.g., can we provide embeddings to free-tier research users but not paid customers?

jordan_legal: yes, potentially. you can offer embeddings to internal teams and research-only users if the platform enforces non-commercial usage and we track it. but we can't enable paid access until we get a license exception. we should avoid any public marketing that implies commercial availability.

kevin: follow-up: what about distillation or training a small student model on generated outputs (distill -> entirely new weights)? does that avoid the redistribution clause?

jordan_legal: depends. some licenses treat derived models trained on model outputs as derivatives too, especially if you used weights to generate a lot of synthetic dataset. Distillation is a legal grey area — we need to get legal approval before pursuing a distillation-as-workaround. do NOT share distillation artifacts externally until signoff.

mike: noted. for timelines: we had a roadmap to ship Boreal embeddings as an experiment next week, and full hosted perf tests in 3 weeks. sounds like we should pause public/paid rollouts.

jordan_legal: action items:
- i will open an upstream permission request today (jordan_legal -> BorealAI) with the template.
- compliance will run risk assessment for embeddings-only offering and draft gating controls for free/research tier.
- eng to freeze any work that packages or hands out quantized weights to customers.
- product to update roadmap to avoid promising commercial availability.

kevin: thanks. i'll add a small note to the PR and mark the quant artifacts as internal-only for now.

sasha: appreciated. please @me on the upstream request thread. if BorealAI grants an exception, we should record the exact scope (commercial vs non-commercial, embeddings allowed, redistribution allowed, attribution text) in the model onboarding checklist. :white_check_mark:

compliance-bot: created ticket LEG-2026-378 with checklist link: https://redwood.internal/legal/requests/LEG-2026-378

jordan_legal: will update here once we hear back.

sasha: ok — holding on any customer-facing work until legal thumbs-up. thanks everyone.
